london.name: London System
london.blurb: You play White and always build the same setup: d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3, Nbd2, Bd3, O-O.

caro.name: Caro-Kann
caro.blurb: You play Black and always build the same setup: ...c6, ...d5, ...Bf5, ...e6, ...Nf6, ...Nbd7, ...Bd6, ...O-O, against 1.e4 and everything else.

london.why: Start with 1.d4: the whole London is built around this pawn.
Develop the dark-squared bishop to f4 BEFORE playing e3, so it isn't shut in.
e3 supports d4 and opens the way for your other bishop.
The knight guards d4 and controls e5.
c3 completes the pawn triangle c3-d4-e3: d4 is now rock-solid.
The b1 knight goes to d2, so the c-pawn can stay on c3; it supports e4 later.
The bishop on d3 aims at h7, Black's weak spot after castling.
Castle: your king is safe and your rook comes into play.

caro.why: ...c6 prepares ...d5, with the c-pawn ready to recapture on d5.
Develop the light-squared bishop to f5 BEFORE ...e6, so it isn't shut in.
Now ...e6 is safe: the bishop is already outside the pawn chain.
The knight develops and fights for e4.
The b8 knight goes to d7, keeping c6 for the pawn and supporting ...e5 or ...c5.
The bishop on d6 challenges White's dark squares and prepares castling.

london.title: Knight to e5, then attack
london.text: Put a knight on e5 (supported by d4 and often f4), then bring the queen to f3 or h5 and push g4-g5 against the black king.

london.title: Bd3 and Qe2/Qc2 aiming at h7
london.text: Your bishop on d3 and a queen on c2 or e2 make a battery on h7. If Black castles kingside, look for Bxh7+ or Ne5 with Qh5.

london.title: e3-e4 central break
london.text: With Qe2, Rfe1 and Rad1, push e4 to open the centre when your pieces are ready. Trade on d5 or c5 first if it helps.

caro.title: Break with ...c5
caro.text: Your pawn chain points to the queenside. Hit White's centre with ...c5 (supported by ...Nc6 and ...Qb6) to attack d4.

caro.title: Minority attack or ...b5-b4
caro.text: If White castles queenside or plays c3, roll your b-pawn forward to open lines on the queenside.

caro.title: Good bishop, safe king
caro.text: Your light-squared bishop is outside the pawn chain. Keep the position closed, castle short, and trade into an endgame where your structure is better.

blacklondon.title: Knight to e4
blacklondon.text: Your setup mirrors the London. Put a knight on e4 (backed by ...f5 if needed), then ...Qf6 or ...Qh4 and ...g5 against a kingside-castled king.

blacklondon.title: Central break ...e5 or ...c5
blacklondon.text: Once you have castled and connected rooks, break with ...c5 or prepare ...e5 to free your position.

blacklondon.title: Queenside space
blacklondon.text: Against c4 setups, keep d5 solid with ...c6 and ...e6, then expand with ...b5 or trade on c4 at the right moment.
